topIssues.title: fix(agent): trigger acknowledgements use host timezone instead of sender timezone
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Post-merge regression

PR #18094 merged as `develop@112a73c8eec7b6491208e6e04d3687482b905e62` while the exact-head timezone blocker remained unresolved: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/18094#pullrequestreview-4890015957

The four relevant blobs (`humanize.ts`, its tests, `trigger.ts`, and its tests) are identical between reviewed head `165f4331b216c48530967f44d259a8e45a8fb1d4` and the merge commit.

## Current behavior

`describeOnceAt` formats the absolute `scheduledAtIso` with process-local `Date.getHours()`, `getDay()`, and calendar constructors. `opCreate` receives the originating `Memory`, but `describeSchedule` receives only the stored trigger config and never resolves `message.content.metadata.uiTimeZone` or the agent `TIMEZONE` setting.

That differs from the canonical `CURRENT_TIME` contract, which resolves:

1. sending-client `metadata.uiTimeZone`;
2. agent `TIMEZONE`;
3. runtime-host timezone.

On a shared or dedicated Cloud agent, host time is not the sending user's time.

## Deterministic reproduction

Pinned Bun `1.3.14`, process `TZ=UTC`:

- now: `2026-08-08T12:00:00.000Z`
- scheduled instant: `2026-08-09T12:00:00.000Z`
- sending user: `America/New_York`
- observed acknowledgement phrase: `tomorrow at 12pm`
- correct user-local phrase: `tomorrow at 8am`

The assertion fails exactly:

```text
Expected: tomorrow at 8am
Received: tomorrow at 12pm
```

The committed formatter suite passes 10/10 and the focused action test passes 1/1 because both construct the target in the test process local timezone. The canonical `CURRENT_TIME` timezone-precedence suite passes 4/4, confirming that the sender-timezone contract already exists elsewhere.

## Impact

The trigger fires at the correct absolute instant, but the verified, action-owned acknowledgement tells Cloud users the wrong clock time and can also misstate the local weekday/date around timezone boundaries.

Historical note: #13509/#13524 addressed a LifeOps owner-fact timezone path, not this `TRIGGER` action acknowledgement path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Resolve the acknowledgement timezone with the canonical client → agent → host precedence.
- Format one-shot clock time, weekday, and date in that resolved IANA timezone without changing the stored `scheduledAtIso` or fire instant.
- Keep cron wording aligned with the timezone in which the scheduler evaluates it; use neutral wording if that timezone cannot be established.
- Add an action-level regression with `host=UTC`, `client=America/New_York`, and an absolute timestamp whose clock time differs.
- Cover a timezone date-boundary case and invalid client-timezone fallback.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud): add gated staging QA session exchange
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Add a disabled-by-default, staging-only API-key → Steward session exchange so the deployed `app-staging.elizacloud.ai` QA lane can authenticate without teaching the browser to accept API keys.
- Require the exact staging environment, host and Origin; exact API-key/user/organization UUID allowlists; the current raw API-key hash from primary storage; active pre-existing user/org/identity/tenant rows; and a 60-second, single-use PKCE code.
- Reject app-scoped and provisioner-managed credentials even if misconfigured into the allowlist. API-key create/detail/regenerate management remains session-only, so one key cannot rotate or rename another key into QA authority.
- Isolate QA codes, signer/kid, token type and caches from ordinary Steward, SSO, OIDC and service-JWT paths. Node, Hono, thin inference, cookie sync and shared-agent scope all revalidate the signed Cloud user/org binding against primary storage with no JIT repair.
- Preserve an absolute one-hour maximum lifetime, reject refresh/token-class laundering, and deploy with an off-first, freshness-checked, rollback-armed cutover. Production has no activation binding.

Relates to #18076 and #18284. This prerequisite does not close either issue: the complete Telegram/Discord shared → dedicated handoff and live staging trajectories remain separate work.

## Safety boundary

- The route is `404` unless every staging-only gate is explicitly configured.
- Production, local, lookalike hosts and non-app-staging Origins fail closed.
- No user, organization, tenant, credential, provider or billable resource is created.
- The source credential never enters a response, browser store, claim or log.
- Codes are opaque, hash-only at rest, short-lived and atomically consumed before signing.
- QA tokens use a dedicated `typ`/`kid`/secret, bypass caches trusted by rollback code, and cannot be accepted as service JWTs even if secrets collide.
- Revocation, same-row key rotation, user/org lifecycle, allowlists, logout and the feature flag are continuously revalidated.

## Verification

- Exact base: `2e60c9a2b6cfbb1b22910ba5dd797d97089ccdc6`; exact head: `2096c0d437cf85bf1687011019543cc29efedd97`.
- Sandboxed Bun `1.3.14`, network denied:

  - Worker health + shared-agent auth scope: **63 pass / 0 fail / 173 assertions**;
  - cutover workflow contract: **4 pass / 0 fail / 37 assertions**.
- Exact `cloud/shared` and `cloud/api` TypeScript checks passed; the two session-only API-key E2E cases use the canonical session cookie and parse cleanly under the isolated harness.
- The cache-rotation regression passes with the CI ambient `CACHE_ENABLED=false`; the isolated suite explicitly enables its in-memory cache and restores the prior environment afterward.
- Biome, actionlint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Router codegen is idempotent: **661 mounted / 0 unconverted**, no generated diff.
- Wrangler `4.100.0` production Worker dry-run passed and exposed no QA activation binding.
- Independent adversarial review of the security implementation returned **GO**, with no remaining P0/P1/P2; the subsequent E2E-only auth-contract alignment is covered by the current exact-head CI.

## Summary

- carry the bot-issued opaque Telegram continuation through provider authentication without trusting browser-supplied Telegram identity
- verify Telegram HMAC/freshness, resolve the prospective account read-only, and acquire an exclusive continuation claim before Telegram or phone mutation
- bind claim, redemption, replay, and completion to the canonical user, organization, Telegram identity, mode, and normalized phone
- make same-identity retries idempotent while rejecting concurrent, stale, cross-account, cross-org, cross-Telegram, and cross-phone attempts
- make an interrupted attempt recoverable: the exact claim holder resumes its own claim after a transient redemption/completion failure, and a leftover claim on a canonically bound session settles into idempotent completed replays
- link the Telegram and phone identity pair atomically across the canonical `users` row and the `user_identities` projection that auth lookups read, with canonical fallback lookups so a stale or absent projection cannot strand an account
- return to Telegram only when the backend authoritatively reports `continuation_redeemed: true`

Closes #17888

## Security invariants

- browser input cannot activate trusted-Telegram mode or assert Telegram identity
- the opaque continuation is excluded from Telegram HMAC verification input
- no durable Telegram or phone mutation occurs before exclusive claim acquisition — including plain session-based linking, which validates phone bindings before the Telegram link
- claim ownership persists through identity mutation and canonical session binding until explicit completion
- elapsed time alone never transfers mutation authority; the exact claim holder (same deterministic claim id, compatible Telegram/phone/account bindings) resumes, while competing claimants receive `409`
- claim lineage is derived from the opaque token, signed Telegram id, and normalized phone — the anonymous first attempt and its post-account-creation retry share one lineage, and the account is bound to the claim record the moment it is known
- the combined Telegram+phone link commits the canonical `users` row and the `user_identities` projection as one transaction; a unique-value collision in either table aborts both writes, so neither table can retain a half-link
- account-bound observation cannot clear another request's active claim
- replay-cache presence is not authorization and signed identity is revalidated before replay
- phone-link failure, phone mismatch, partial user/org binding, or malformed successful claim JSON fail closed

## Review follow-ups

Current stack: `9a79c01be` (original) → `cc873f030` (claim resumability) → `ed887a0f1` (atomic identity linking) → `84a4bc0b8` (e2e bot-id fixture) → `ec48c139c` (landing composer test budget) → `d5acbd5df` (identity projection atomicity) → `34ca68a1c` (projection boundary consolidated) → `506ad2cc5` (verified-phone guard + typed link boundary) → `cc591dbf8` (gateway router stale-identity transition guard).

**First blocking review (claim-holder deadlock) — addressed in `cc873f030`:**

- `claimContinuation` resumes the exact holder (same claim id + compatible bindings) instead of `409`; competing claim ids and mismatched Telegram/phone/account bindings remain `409`
- a leftover claim on a canonically bound session is cleared by its own lineage and settles into completed replays, covering a crash between redemption and completion
- `createContinuationClaimId` drops account material so the anonymous create-then-retry transition hashes to the same lineage; the claim record itself carries the account binding once known
- the write-only `expiresAt` lease field is removed; time-based takeover remains impossible in both directions (pinned against legacy records still carrying the field)
- plain session-based linking validates phone bindings before any durable link; the strict-continuation identity assertion no longer early-outs for trusted transports; the redemption idempotency key includes the continuation token
- integrated regression composes the real auth route with the real coordinator Durable Objects: transient redemption failure → identical signed retry redeems exactly once; anonymous create-then-retry resumes with a stable claim id; crash between redemption and completion resolves without re-redeeming

**Second blocking review (stale `user_identities` projection) — addressed in `d5acbd5df`, consolidated in `34ca68a1c`:**

- `usersRepository.linkTelegramAndPhoneIdentity` commits the canonical `users` update and an authoritative `user_identities` upsert in ONE transaction; the projection mirrors the freshly returned canonical row, a missing projection row is inserted, and a unique collision in either table rolls back both — neither table can retain a half-link
- `linkTelegramAndPhoneToUser` routes through that boundary (the service-level test proves no separate canonical update is issued around it)
- direct auth/routing lookups remain projection-authoritative; the write-side upsert (rather than read-side fallbacks) is what prevents drift from stranding an account into the create-collide-500 chain
- repository-level regression against the real Drizzle schema (`pushSchema` on isolated PGlite): (1) link then fresh lookups resolve the user by both Telegram ID and phone; (2) a stale cross-user projection collision rolls the canonical write back with no half-link in either table; (3) a legacy user without a projection row gets one created by the link

## Verification

Gates run on macOS arm64 with the pinned toolchain (Bun 1.3.14, Node 24.15.0); focused suites, API build, and Biome re-run green at `506ad2cc5`; gateway-webhook identity/e2e suites green at `cc591dbf8` (18 tests, 84 assertions).

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| cloud-api focused suites (route / integration / coordinator / platform-caller) | 39 passed (11+3+15+10), 0 failed |
| cloud-shared focused suites (identity-link integration regression / user-service error-policy / onboarding-chat / host-contract) | 58 passed, 0 failed under `bun test --isolate` |
| Cloud API TypeScript build (`tsc6 --noEmit`) | passed |
| Homepage typecheck + production build | passed (surfaces unchanged by the cloud-only commits; Chromium suite green at this lineage) |
| Chromium Telegram return coverage | 3 passed (with and without `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT_ID` in the shell, exercising the `84a4bc0b8` fixture) |
| Scoped Biome over changed files | passed, no fixes applied |
| `git diff --check` | passed |
| Root `bun run verify` | passed (exit 0) at `34ca68a1c` and `506ad2cc5`; re-run at `cc591dbf8` in progress at body-update time |

Chromium command used `VITE_TELEGRAM_BOT_ID=123456789` as an explicit fake test fixture; Telegram and Cloud API responses were intercepted locally. A real staging `/start` → provider callback → canonical redemption → bot-return run remains a deployment/release gate because this checkout does not have staging secrets or deployment authority.

topPRs.author: wtfsayo
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

No linked issue was created before this work began. This PR is the acceptance record for the Settings → Connectors migration.

Definition of Done: [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] Targets `develop`; branch rebases/merges from `develop` have remained conflict-free.
- [ ] Full `bun run verify` and required visual evidence are still pending.
- [x] Focused behavior is covered by deterministic tests listed below.

# Contribution provenance

<!-- contribution-attribution:v1 -->
<!-- attribution-row:ai-assistance -->
- AI assistance: `yes`
<!-- attribution-row:models -->
- Model(s) used: `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`
<!-- attribution-row:client -->
- Agent tooling: `pi`
<!-- attribution-row:skill-revision -->
- Skill path: `N/A - no contribution skill used`
<!-- attribution-row:status -->
- Provenance status: `self-reported`

# Summary

Migrates **Settings → Connectors** from inline accordions to a dense index/detail workflow:

- Grouped connector index with a persisted **Delegate / Bot** identity lens.
- Per-connector routes at `#connectors/<id>` with browser/hardware Back support.
- Connector enable/load switch first; duplicate schema-level `Enabled` fields are hidden.
- One config item per row.
- Text, number, secret, JSON, array, code, and multiline values rest as value chips and open a **Save / Cancel** dialog.
- Dialog Save stages edits locally; **Save changes / Cancel** commits or discards the complete bundle atomically.
- Signal and WhatsApp QR states use the same description-left/action-right pattern as other connectors.
- Required fields use badges without decorative left bars.
- Stronger contrast for primary/disabled CTAs, neutral actions, and value chips.
- Deep links and programmatic connector focus remain supported.

# Identity classification

Declared setup modes are filtered by identity. Plugin-managed inventories are filtered from each stored account record—not the catalog creation default:

- `OWNER` → Delegate
- `AGENT` → Bot
- `TEAM` or unknown role → visible in both lenses

| Connector | Delegate | Bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discord | Desktop App | OAuth Gateway, Bot Token |
| Telegram | Personal Account; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Cloud Gateway, Bot Token; stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| Slack | Stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | OAuth App, Socket Mode; stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| X | OAuth, local OAuth2, developer tokens; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| Signal | QR-linked account; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| WhatsApp | QR-linked personal account; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Business Cloud API; stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| iMessage | iPhone gateway, direct chat.db, BlueBubbles | Blooio cloud number |
| BlueBubbles | Cloud and local owner bridge | — |

Single-form fallback classifications:

- **Bot:** Bluesky, Farcaster, Nostr, Matrix, MS Teams, Mattermost, Google Chat, Feishu, LINE, Zalo Official, Tlon, Nextcloud Talk, Twitch, Blooio.
- **Delegate:** Instagram, Zalo User, Google Workspace.
- Unknown third-party connectors intentionally remain visible in both lenses.

## Known identity ambiguities

The following plugins do not declare account ownership strongly enough to classify every credential with certainty:

- Slack Socket Mode still includes optional `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` in an otherwise bot-oriented schema.
- Tlon credentials can represent an agent ship or the owner’s ship.
- Matrix credentials can represent a dedicated bot user or an owner account.
- Instagram supports personal, brand, and bot-like profiles.
- Bluesky app passwords can technically belong to either identity.
- X OAuth2 and OAuth1 modes remain one same-lens schema; this is setup-mode leakage, not a Delegate/Bot error.

# Review fixes included

- Atomic bundle save prevents overlapping plugin restarts and stale-completion draft loss.
- Failed saves retain drafts; duplicate Save clicks are ignored.
- Configured secrets cannot be deleted by empty Save/Enter.
- Optional secrets retain an explicit confirmed **Clear → Clear value** path.
- Masked secret chips have distinct accessible names (`Edit <field>`).
- User-opened detail routes use `pushState`; visible Back consumes that entry. Programmatic/deep-linked details retain replace semantics.
- Default-backed iMessage policy controls no longer require optional CLI/database path overrides.
- Mixed plugin-managed OWNER/AGENT records are separated by actual stored role; TEAM/unknown remain neutral.
- Programmatic detail→detail focus preserves the user-pushed history marker so visible Back then hardware Back leave the connectors stack cleanly.
- Catalog-backed detail modes follow the same `connectorSupportsChannelMode` lens policy as the index (e.g. Google under Bot does not expose plugin-managed inventory).
- Mobile detail hides the in-content Back control; ViewHeader remains the sole mobile Back target (`hidden` / `md:inline-flex`, `min-h-11`).

# Risks

**Medium.** This changes shared config-field and button primitives plus connector routing/history. Primary risks are incorrect identity filtering, lost config drafts, accidental secret deletion, and duplicate history entries. Focused tests cover each path; visual evidence and full repository verification remain outstanding.

# Testing

## Automated

- [x] UI focused suite: **6 files / focused connector routing/history/config tests passed** (re-run after re-review)
  - lens and mode filtering
  - mixed OWNER/AGENT/TEAM/unknown account records
  - atomic multi-field saves, duplicate saves, stale completions, failures, and Cancel
  - secret accessible names, empty-save safety, and confirmed deletion
  - QR action-row states
  - browser and visible-Back history behavior
  - duplicate field hiding and structured-value dialogs
- [x] iMessage manifest regression: **1 test passed**
- [x] `bun run --cwd packages/ui typecheck`
- [x] `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-imessage typecheck`
- [x] Biome checks for touched files
- [x] `git diff --check`

## Reviewer walkthrough

1. Open Settings → Connectors and switch Delegate/Bot.
2. Open Discord, Telegram, Slack, Signal, WhatsApp, iMessage, and BlueBubbles details.
3. Confirm only identity-appropriate modes/accounts appear.
4. Edit two config values; verify they stage before one atomic Save changes action.
5. Open a configured optional secret; verify empty Save is disabled and Clear requires confirmation.
6. Navigate index → detail → visible Back → browser/hardware Back; verify each history level is consumed once.

# Evidence Gate

topPRs.title: feat(plugin-taskmarket): delegate work to the TaskMarket marketplace
topPRs.author: jvkassi
topPRs.body:
## What

Adds `@elizaos/plugin-taskmarket` — lets an Eliza agent delegate a request to an external worker paid in USDC on Base ([TaskMarket](https://taskmarket.dev/)) instead of spending more inference on work another worker can do.

Three actions:

| Action | Spends? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TASKMARKET_BROWSE` | no | list / get open tasks |
| `TASKMARKET_STATUS` | no | balance, reputation, own submissions |
| `TASKMARKET_CREATE_TASK` | **yes** | post a task (escrows real USDC) |

## Safety

`TASKMARKET_CREATE_TASK` is the only money-moving action, gated three independent ways:

1. `TASKMARKET_ALLOW_TASK_CREATION` — off by default.
2. `TASKMARKET_MAX_TASK_REWARD_USDC` — enforced **by refusal**, never by silently trimming the reward. Hard-capped at 50.
3. `userConfirmed` — must come from direct user approval, not from model-generated content.

The disabled check is duplicated in `validate()` and at handler entry on purpose: `validate()` keeps the tool off the planner's list, the handler check is the backstop against a hallucinated call. Every guard failure returns **before** the network call — the tests assert `fetch` was never invoked on each rejection path.

No action accepts a submission or releases escrow. Settlement stays with the human. Error text never echoes the bearer token or the request URL (which carries the caller's address).

## Notes from integrating against the live API

- The `/api` base-path prefix is mandatory; every path 404s without it.
- The bearer token does **not** identify the caller — account routes need an explicit `address` query param, hence the separate required `TASKMARKET_ADDRESS` setting.
- Amounts are atomic 6-decimal USDC everywhere except `/wallet/balance`. Converted at the client boundary; actions speak whole USDC.
- Task descriptions run 2–10 KB, so list output truncates (`TASKMARKET_LIST_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`) to keep a full board listing from eating the context window.

## Testing

```
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-taskmarket test        # 16 passed
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-taskmarket typecheck   # no errors in this package
```

Unit tests mock `fetch`, which validates this plugin's logic but not the vendor's URL shape — so it was also verified with a **read-only live run** against `api.taskmarket.dev` (balance, task list, task detail, submissions), plus live confirmation that all three creation guards refuse before any POST. Task creation itself is never exercised in tests; it escrows real funds.
